title: Shoulder and Wrist Activation
description: A seated dynamic warm-up targeting the shoulders, wrists and forearms that carry almost all the load in wheelchair basketball, done before any pushing begins.

content.objective: Prepare the shoulders, wrists and forearms for the repeated loading of pushing and shooting.
content.setup: Players sit in a loose group with enough space to swing their arms freely.
instructions: Circle both shoulders forward for 10 reps, then backward for 10 reps.
Make loose fists and circle the wrists in both directions for 10 reps each.
Reach both arms overhead and across the body for a gentle stretch, holding each for 10 seconds.
Finish with 20 seconds of light, easy shadow pushes to raise the heart rate.
coachingPoints: Keep the movements controlled, not fast and loose.
Breathe normally throughout rather than holding the breath.
Build the range of motion gradually across the set.
commonMistakes: Rushing through to get to the ball work sooner.
Skipping the wrist work, which matters as much as the shoulders.
Rushing through the movements instead of using the full range of motion.
content.safety: Stop any stretch that causes sharp pain and tell the coach.
